$note: Pofu's material library (look round 3; colour script v1, docs/design/colour-script.md; docs/research/pro-game-craft.md section 4.4). Each recurring material's local colour: its colour under neutral light, as CIELAB hue (degrees) and chroma ranges. Light is added at runtime by the colour script (design/art/colour-script.json), so assets arrive unlit and these ranges describe paint, not light. harmony.py measures every material that has a 'detect' block on the assets in its 'regions', and corrects only when the generator drifted OUT of the range, back to its nearest edge: it never moves a material toward another one. 'accent' materials may leave a cell's gamut, within 'max_area' of the frame. Change a range only with the teapot or harmony sheet in the PR.

rose-copper.$note: The çaydanlık, the lantern cap, the tray. Pink-leaning, never brass: the founder found the original rose copper prettier than round 2's warm shift (2026-11-02). The kettle reads warm at night because the ember lights it (the colour script's practical pool), not because it was repainted. #D4875F with copper-light #EFB28E highlights.

detect.$note: Hue alone cannot separate copper (H 50-58) from honey wood (H 56-72), so the material is measured inside a region of each canvas (x0, y0, x1, y1 as fractions, feathered).

honey-wood.$note: Stalls, the workshop, the windmill's cap: yellower and duller than the copper, so the two separate by hue and by response.

sage-lawn.$note: Large area: inside the cell's gamut always; takes the fill strongly in shadow.

pofu-fur.$note: Hero by value, not chroma. Char-guarded: measured, never corrected, never desaturated by the grade (the colour script's character light).

practical-light.$note: The ember, the lantern, the door's round window: emissive, never graded, lights its neighbours.
